d.d: A round sweet and juicy stone fruit, resembling peach or plum in taste, with a yellow-orange flesh, lightly fuzzy skin and a large seed inside.
A pale yellow-orange colour, like that of an apricot fruit.
Of a pale yellowish-orange colour, like that of an apricot.
The fourth month of the Gregorian calendar, following March and preceding May.
A female given name transferred from the month name [in turn from English]; used since the early 20th century.
An article of clothing worn over the front of the torso and/or legs for protection from spills; also historically worn by Freemasons and as part of women's fashion.
d.x: She tied an apron around her waist before cooking dinner.

d.d: The short cassock ordinarily worn by English bishops.
The paved area of an airport, especially the area where aircraft park away from a terminal.
d.x: The plane was parked on the airport apron.

d.d: To cover with, or as if with, an apron.
Of an appropriate or pertinent nature.
Regarding, concerning, in regard to, on the subject of.
